Code 
# All summaries are finite-only: non-finite estimates/bounds (e.g. from Cox
# separation or an unstable small-B IJ) are dropped so a single blow-up cannot
# dominate a mean.
.cover <- function(target, lo, hi) {
  target <- rep_len(target, length(lo))   # recycle scalar targets (CDE/marginal) to n reps
  ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  mean(target[ok] >= lo[ok] & target[ok] <= hi[ok])
}
.pbias <- function(est, target) {
  d <- (est - target) / target; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
  if (!length(d)) return(NA_real_)
  100 * mean(d)
}
.mfin <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_ }
.sdfin <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x) > 1L) sd(x) else NA_real_ }
# Empirical (true) SD on the log-HR (beta) scale: SD of log(HR) across reps.
.sd_log <- function(e) { l <- log(e[is.finite(e) & e > 0]); if (length(l) > 1L) sd(l) else NA_real_ }
# Stored per-replicate log-HR (beta-scale) SE for an estimator -- read at the
# source, never back-calculated from CI bounds (or_/nv_/fb_*_se; MR uses its IJ
# SE, mr_*_se_ij).  A missing column (results saved before SEs were stored)
# yields all-NA so the table still renders.
.get_se <- function(r, k, suffix) {
  col <- if (k == "fld") paste0("fld_", suffix, "_se")
         else if (k == "mr") paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_se_ij")
         else if (k == "mrw") paste0("mr_", suffix, "_se_w")
         else if (k == "mrwf") paste0("mr_", suffix, "_se_wf")
         else paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_se")
  v <- r[[col]]
  if (is.null(v)) rep(NA_real_, nrow(r)) else v
}

# Estimator rows for one block.  FB appears whenever fb_* data exist (run OR
# joined); MR (field) appears wherever that block's field columns are present
# and finite -- the Hhat block always under ci_method = "field", the Hhat^c
# block only when the render ran with field_complement = TRUE
# (TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06) -- and uses est2 with the two-sided
# quantile interval as its primary interval (decision F4).
# The two winner-only IJ rows (TASK_complement_refinements_2026-09-06) share
# MR (IJ)'s point estimate and differ only in SE/bounds; they appear when
# the bundle recorded mr_<block>_se_w.
est_keys_for <- function(r, suffix) {
  keys <- c(oracle = "or", naive = "nv", FB = "fb",
            `MR (IJ)` = "mr", `MR (IJ, winner)` = "mrw",
            `MR (IJ, winner-floor)` = "mrwf", `MR (field)` = "fld")
  if (!any(is.finite(r$fb_H_est))) keys <- keys[names(keys) != "FB"]
  if (!any(is.finite(r[[paste0("fld_", suffix, "_est2")]] %||% NA_real_)))
    keys <- keys[names(keys) != "MR (field)"]
  if (!isTRUE(show_winner_rows) ||
      !any(is.finite(r[[paste0("mr_", suffix, "_se_w")]] %||% NA_real_)))
    keys <- keys[!names(keys) %in% c("MR (IJ, winner)", "MR (IJ, winner-floor)")]
  keys
}
.est_cols <- function(r, k, suffix) {
  if (k == "fld") list(e  = r[[paste0("fld_", suffix, "_est2")]],
                       lo = r[[paste0("fld_", suffix, "_lo2s")]],
                       hi = r[[paste0("fld_", suffix, "_hi2s")]])
  else if (k %in% c("mrw", "mrwf")) {
    vs <- if (k == "mrw") "_w" else "_wf"
    list(e  = r[[paste0("mr_", suffix, "_est")]],
         lo = r[[paste0("mr_", suffix, "_lo", vs)]],
         hi = r[[paste0("mr_", suffix, "_hi", vs)]])
  }
  else list(e  = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_est")]],
            lo = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_lo")]],
            hi = r[[paste0(k, "_", suffix, "_hi")]])
}

# Build one block (H or Hc): estimator rows against the four targets.
build_block <- function(r, suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
  est_keys <- est_keys_for(r, suffix)
  or_est <- r[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]   # per-replicate oracle target
  bH_est <- r[[paste0("betaHhat_", suffix)]]     # per-replicate beta(Hhat) target
  rows <- lapply(names(est_keys), function(lab) {
    k  <- est_keys[[lab]]
    ec <- .est_cols(r, k, suffix)
    e  <- ec$e
    lo <- ec$lo
    hi <- ec$hi
    len <- hi - lo; len <- len[is.finite(len)]
    seb <- .get_se(r, k, suffix)                  # stored log-HR (beta) SE
    data.frame(
      Estimator = lab,
      n       = sum(is.finite(e)),
      Avg     = .mfin(e),
      SD        = .sd_log(e),                      # empirical SD, log-HR (beta) scale  [reported]
      SD_hr     = .sdfin(e),                       # empirical SD, HR scale             [retained]
      SD_hat    = .mfin(seb),                      # mean model SE, log-HR (beta) scale [reported]
      SD_hat_hr = .mfin(e * seb),                  # mean model SE, HR scale            [retained]
      Length  = if (length(len)) mean(len) else NA_real_,
      b_oracle = .pbias(e, or_est),
      b_betaHhat = .pbias(e, bH_est),
      b_cde    = .pbias(e, tgt_cde),
      b_marg   = .pbias(e, tgt_marg),
      Cov_oracle = .cover(or_est, lo, hi),
      Cov_betaHhat = .cover(bH_est, lo, hi),
      Cov_cde    = .cover(tgt_cde,  lo, hi),
      Cov_marg   = .cover(tgt_marg, lo, hi),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  # FB rows render whenever fb_* data exist -- computed (fb_mode "run") or
  # adopted from the committed bundle (fb_mode "join").  run_fb alone cannot
  # gate this: it is FALSE under "join".
  fb_in_tables <- any(is.finite(results$fb_H_est))
  rH  <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  blockH  <- build_block(rH, "H",  truth$cde_H,  truth$marg_H)
  blockHc <- build_block(rH, "Hc", truth$cde_Hc, truth$marg_Hc)
  # Fold the mean identified subgroup size into the block label, so |H-hat|
  # travels with the table (as in build_estimation_table()'s row-group labels).
  .blk_lab <- function(label, sym, v) {
    if (!any(is.finite(v))) return(label)
    sprintf("%s (mean |%s| = %.0f, %.1f%% ITT)", label, sym,
            mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), 100 * mean(v, na.rm = TRUE) / n_sample)
  }
  est_tab <- rbind(
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Harm  \u0124", "\u0124", rH$n_harm), blockH),
    cbind(Block = .blk_lab("Complement  \u0124\u1d9c", "\u0124\u1d9c",
                           n_sample - rH$n_harm), blockHc)
  )

  det_rate <- mean(results$detected, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Classification + decision + IJ-stability diagnostics (over detected reps).
  cls <- sprintf("sens %.2f \u00b7 spec %.2f \u00b7 PPV %.2f \u00b7 NPV %.2f",
                 .mfin(rH$sens), .mfin(rH$spec), .mfin(rH$ppv), .mfin(rH$npv))
  # MR availability: the share of DETECTED reps for which MR returned an object.
  # The detected-only denominator is what makes this mean "MR failed" rather than
  # "nothing was found": .na_record() sets mr_ok = 0L, so every undetected rep
  # also carries mr_ok = 0 and an unconditional mean would just reproduce the
  # detection rate.  Reported because mr_ok is otherwise invisible -- a run where
  # MR failed on a third of the detected reps would read identically to one where
  # it never failed.
  mr_avail  <- mean(rH$mr_ok, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Both of the following are ALREADY conditional on MR having run: mr_harm_flag
  # and ij_source stay NA when g is NULL, and na.rm = TRUE drops those reps.  So
  # their denominator is mr_avail * |detected|, not |detected| -- which is why
  # availability is stated first and these two read "among those".
  harm_rate <- mean(rH$mr_harm_flag, na.rm = TRUE)
  ij_ok     <- mean(rH$ij_source == "ij", na.rm = TRUE)

  gt(est_tab, groupname_col = "Block") |>
    tab_header(
      title = if (fb_in_tables)
        "FB vs MR (IJ) vs MR (field): estimation & coverage"
      else "MR (IJ) vs MR (field): estimation & coverage",
      subtitle = sprintf("hr=%.2f \u00b7 n=%d, %d sims, draws=%d \u00b7 fb_mode=%s \u00b7 resample identification",
                         target_hr_harm, n_sample, n_sims, mr_draws, fb_mode)) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Avg, SD, SD_hr, SD_hat, SD_hat_hr, Length), decimals = 2) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg), decimals = 1) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg), decimals = 2) |>
    cols_label(
      n = "n",
      SD = md("$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$"), SD_hat = md("$\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$"),
      b_oracle = md("$b^{\\text{or}}$"), b_betaHhat = md("$b^{\\beta}$"),
      b_cde = md("$b^{\\ddagger}$"), b_marg = md("$b^{\\dagger}$"),
      Cov_oracle = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\text{or}}$"), Cov_betaHhat = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\beta}$"),
      Cov_cde = md("$\\hat{C}^{\\ddagger}$"), Cov_marg = md("$C^{\\dagger}$")) |>
    cols_hide(columns = c(SD_hr, SD_hat_hr)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "Relative bias (%)", columns = c(b_oracle, b_betaHhat, b_cde, b_marg)) |>
    tab_spanner(label = "95% coverage", columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg)) |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(sprintf(
      "Detection rate **%.0f%%** of %d sims; MR returned an estimate on **%.0f%%** of detected reps; among those, MR flags harm in **%.0f%%** and IJ variance held (not fallback) in **%.0f%%**. Classification of \u0124 vs true subgroup: %s. Summaries finite-only over detected reps; `n` = finite reps contributing.",
      100 * det_rate, n_sims, 100 * mr_avail, 100 * harm_rate, 100 * ij_ok, cls))) |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "$\\text{SD}_{\\beta}$ (empirical SD) and $\\widehat{\\text{SD}}_{\\beta}$ (mean of the model SEs) are on the log-hazard-ratio ($\\beta$) scale; HR-scale versions are computed but hidden.",
      "Targets: $b^{\\text{or}}$ vs per-replicate oracle $\\hat\\theta(H)$;",
      "$b^{\\beta}$ / $\\hat C^{\\beta}$ vs the conditional subgroup HR $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ at the realized region (Theorem 2 target);",
      "$b^{\\ddagger}$ vs CDE $\\theta^{\\ddagger}$;",
      "$b^{\\dagger}$ vs marginal subgroup HR $\\theta^{\\dagger}$.",
      "`Length` = mean CI length.",
      if (fb_in_tables)
        "FB = `H2` (León Eq.7, both bias sources); MR (IJ) = de-biased estimate with IJ interval; MR (field) = shrunk-field `est2` with the two-sided 95% Lambda-quantile interval (its SE column is the Lambda-SD `se_field`). The field is computed for the Hhat block only (F3); Hhat-c stays on the IJ interval."
      else
        "MR (IJ) = de-biased estimate with IJ interval; MR (field) = shrunk-field `est2` with the two-sided 95% Lambda-quantile interval (its SE column is the Lambda-SD `se_field`); field is Hhat-block only (F3). FB absent in this cell/range.")))

# Median companion to the main (mean-based) table, rendered the SAME way -- a
# single auto-printed gt -- so the column formatting matches exactly.  Reuses

if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {

  .medfin     <- function(x) { x <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(x)) stats::median(x) else NA_real_ }
  .pbias_med  <- function(est, target) {
    d <- (est - target) / target; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
    if (!length(d)) return(NA_real_)
    100 * stats::median(d)
  }

  build_block_med <- function(r, suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
    est_keys <- est_keys_for(r, suffix)   # same roster as the mean table
    or_est <- r[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]

    rows <- lapply(names(est_keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- est_keys[[lab]]
      ec <- .est_cols(r, k, suffix)
      e  <- ec$e
      lo <- ec$lo
      hi <- ec$hi
      len <- hi - lo; len <- len[is.finite(len)]
      seb <- .get_se(r, k, suffix)                  # stored log-HR (beta) SE
      data.frame(
        Estimator = lab,
        n       = sum(is.finite(e)),
        Med     = .medfin(e),
        SD        = .sd_log(e),                      # empirical SD, log-HR (beta) scale  [reported]
        SD_hr     = .sdfin(e),                       # empirical SD, HR scale             [retained]
        SD_hat    = .medfin(seb),                    # median model SE, log-HR (beta)     [reported]
        SD_hat_hr = .medfin(e * seb),                # median model SE, HR scale          [retained]
        Length  = if (length(len)) stats::median(len) else NA_real_,
        b_oracle = .pbias_med(e, or_est),
        b_betaHhat = .pbias_med(e, bH_est),
        b_cde    = .pbias_med(e, tgt_cde),
        b_marg   = .pbias_med(e, tgt_marg),
        Cov_oracle = .cover(or_est, lo, hi),
        Cov_betaHhat = .cover(bH_est, lo, hi),
        Cov_cde    = .cover(tgt_cde,  lo, hi),
        Cov_marg   = .cover(tgt_marg, lo, hi),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    })
    do.call(rbind, rows)
  }

  rHm <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]

    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov_oracle, Cov_betaHhat, Cov_cde, Cov_marg), decimals = 2) |>
    cols_label(

                            .bH, truth$marg_H)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

13 The conditional target \(\beta(\widehat H)\) vs the oracle

Code 
# Narrative companion to the estimation tables: summarises the new conditional
# target beta(Hhat) and contrasts it with the oracle.  Pure consumer of `results`
# (no simulation), reusing the table's per-replicate relative-bias / coverage
# logic, restricted to the harm block where the contrast lives.
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results)) {
  rC <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  ok <- is.finite(rC$betaHhat_H)
  if (any(ok)) {
    .relb <- function(est, tgt) { d <- (est - tgt) / tgt; d <- d[is.finite(d)]
                                  if (length(d)) 100 * mean(d) else NA_real_ }
    .covg <- function(tgt, lo, hi) { o <- is.finite(tgt) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
                                     if (any(o)) 100 * mean(tgt[o] >= lo[o] & tgt[o] <= hi[o]) else NA_real_ }
    bH  <- rC$betaHhat_H        # realized-region truth (the Theorem 2 target)
    orH <- rC$or_H_est         # oracle: effect at the TRUE region (theta-dagger(H))
    keys <- c(naive = "nv", FB = "fb", MR = "mr")
    if (!run_fb) keys <- keys[names(keys) != "FB"]
    erows <- vapply(names(keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- keys[[lab]]
      e  <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_est")]]; lo <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_lo")]]; hi <- rC[[paste0(k, "_H_hi")]]
      sprintf("| %s | %.2f | %+.0f%% | %+.0f%% | %.0f%% | %.0f%% |",
              lab, mean(e[is.finite(e)]), .relb(e, bH), .relb(e, orH),
              .covg(bH, lo, hi), .covg(orH, lo, hi))
    }, character(1))
    mr_m   <- mean(rC$mr_H_est[is.finite(rC$mr_H_est)])
    nearer <- if (isTRUE(abs(mr_m - mean(orH, na.rm = TRUE)) <= abs(mr_m - mean(bH))))
                "the oracle (true-region) effect $\\theta^{\\dagger}(H)$" else "$\\beta(\\widehat H)$"

    cat(sprintf("\n::: {.callout-note title=\"The \u03b2(\u0124) target vs the oracle \u2014 harm block, %d detections\"}\n\n", sum(ok)))
    cat("$\\beta(\\widehat H)$ is the population value of the standard within-subgroup analysis ",
        "(the Cox hazard ratio of treatment) at the **realized** region $\\widehat H$ \u2014 the truth of the ",
        "subgroup the search actually found, and the conditional estimand Theorem 2 certifies. It is a ",
        "*per-replicate* target. The **oracle** $\\hat\\theta(H)$ refits on the **true** region $H$ instead ",
        "(the effect one would estimate knowing the subgroup); their gap is the price of selecting the ",
        "wrong region.\n\n", sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("- $\\beta(\\widehat H)$: mean **%.2f** (median %.2f)  \u00b7  $\\beta(\\widehat H^{c})$: mean %.2f\n",
                mean(bH), stats::median(bH), mean(rC$betaHhat_Hc[is.finite(rC$betaHhat_Hc)])))
    cat(sprintf("- oracle $\\hat\\theta(H)$: mean **%.2f**  (true-region effect $\\theta^{\\dagger}(H) = %.2f$)\n",
                mean(orH, na.rm = TRUE), truth$marg_H))
    cat(sprintf("- discovery gap $\\hat\\theta(H) - \\beta(\\widehat H)$: mean **%.2f**\n\n",
                mean((orH - bH)[is.finite(orH - bH)])))
    cat("| estimator | mean | bias vs $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ | bias vs oracle | cov $\\beta(\\widehat H)$ | cov oracle |\n")
    cat("|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|\n")
    cat(paste(erows, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
    cat(sprintf("In this cell the MR estimate sits nearer %s. ", nearer))
    cat("The *bias vs $\\beta(\\widehat H)$* column is what Theorem 2 speaks to; *bias vs oracle* is distance ",
        "from the true-region effect. ", sep = "")
    cat(sprintf("At %d detections these figures are indicative, not a coverage read.\n", sum(ok)))
    cat("\n:::\n\n")
  }
}

14 Paired FB ↔︎ MR agreement panel

For a fixed candidate family (consistency) both procedures correct the same selected \(\hat H\) on the same data, so per-replicate differences isolate the dfbeta linearisation – the cleanest test of the leading-order correspondence. For dina/grf the FB bootstrap regenerates the family (and re-selects) on each resample while MR holds the observed family fixed, so the differences additionally carry the family-regeneration gap (unconditional vs conditional-on-family). Reported on the log-effect scale.

Code 
# Runs whenever fb_* data exist -- computed (fb_mode "run") or joined from the
# committed bundle (fb_mode "join"); run_fb alone cannot gate it.
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && any(is.finite(results$fb_H_est))) {
  rd <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]

  # Per-block log-scale agreement (comparator - FB) on point estimate and
  # bounds.  mr_cols selects the comparator: the MR (IJ) columns, or the
  # MR (field) est2 with its quantile interval (task 1a: the agreement panel
  # gains est2; field exists for the Hhat block only, F3).
  agree_block <- function(suffix, mr_cols = c("mr_%s_est", "mr_%s_lo", "mr_%s_hi"),
                          comparator = "MR (IJ)") {
    e1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_est")]]; e2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[1], suffix)]]
    l1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_lo")]];  l2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[2], suffix)]]
    u1 <- rd[[paste0("fb_", suffix, "_hi")]];  u2 <- rd[[sprintf(mr_cols[3], suffix)]]
    ok <- is.finite(e1) & is.finite(e2)
    if (sum(ok) < 2L) return(NULL)
    blk <- sprintf("%s \u00b7 %s",
                   if (suffix == "H") "Harm \u0124" else "Complement \u0124\u1d9c",
                   comparator)
    dpt <- log(e2[ok]) - log(e1[ok])
    dlo <- log(l2[ok]) - log(l1[ok]); dhi <- log(u2[ok]) - log(u1[ok])
    list(
      tab = data.frame(
        Block = blk,
        Quantity = c("log point", "log CI lower", "log CI upper"),
        mean_d = c(mean(dpt), .mfin(dlo), .mfin(dhi)),
        sd_d   = c(sd(dpt),   .sdfin(dlo), .sdfin(dhi)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
      n = sum(ok), corr = suppressWarnings(cor(log(e1[ok]), log(e2[ok]))),
      pts = data.frame(block = blk, fb = e1[ok], mr = e2[ok])
    )
  }

  aH  <- agree_block("H"); aHc <- agree_block("Hc")
  aHf <- agree_block("H", mr_cols = c("fld_%s_est2", "fld_%s_lo2s", "fld_%s_hi2s"),
                     comparator = "MR (field) est2")
  parts <- Filter(Negate(is.null), list(aH, aHc, aHf))

  if (length(parts)) {
    tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "tab"))
    sub <- paste(vapply(parts, function(p)
      sprintf("%s: %d reps, corr %.3f", p$tab$Block[1], p$n, p$corr),
      character(1)), collapse = "  \u00b7  ")
    cat(as_raw_html(
      gt(tab, groupname_col = "Block") |>
        tab_header(title = "MR \u2212 FB (log scale)", subtitle = sub) |>
        cols_label(mean_d = "Mean \u0394", sd_d = "SD \u0394") |>
        fmt_number(columns = c(mean_d, sd_d), decimals = 4)
    ))

    pts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, `[[`, "pts"))
    p <- ggplot(pts, aes(x = fb, y = mr)) +
      geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
      geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
      facet_wrap(~ block, scales = "free") +
      labs(x = expression("FB  "*hat(theta)^"*"),
           y = expression("MR  "*tilde(theta)),
           title = "Per-replicate de-biased point estimates") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
    print(p)
  } else {
    cat("Too few paired replicates at smoke-test counts to draw the panel.\n")
  }
}

15 MR (field) diagnostics

The field-calibrated interval’s own summaries (task TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05, Stage 3 layout): two-sided 95% coverage with Wilson intervals (the paper’s primary convention, F4), one-sided lower coverage as the supplementary read, retained bias of the de-biased estimate \(\tilde\beta\) and the shrunk-field est2 against the conditional target \(\beta(\widehat H)\) (log-HR and SD units), the \(\lambda\)-SD/SD calibration ratio, and the Monte Carlo draw-usage counts.

When the render ran with field_complement = TRUE (FS_S7_FIELD_COMPLEMENT=TRUE; TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06) the same summaries follow for the complement \(\widehat H^{c}\), evaluated on the same outer/inner draws and winners as the harm field with the complement’s own influence. Its exposed limit is the upper bound (a benefit claim “HR in \(\widehat H^{c}\) is at most \(U\)”): the one-sided coverage in the complement block is \(\beta(\widehat H^{c}) \le U\) for every estimator, and the display uses side = "upper".

Code 
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && any(is.finite(results$fld_H_est2))) {
  rF <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]

  # Wilson 95% interval for a coverage proportion (paper convention).
  .wilson <- function(x, n, z = qnorm(0.975)) {
    if (!is.finite(x) || !is.finite(n) || n <= 0) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
    ctr <- (x + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
    hw  <- z * sqrt(x * (1 - x) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
    c(ctr - hw, ctr + hw)
  }
  .cov_n <- function(target, lo, hi) {           # coverage + its denominator
    target <- rep_len(target, length(lo))
    ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(lo) & is.finite(hi)
    if (!any(ok)) return(c(NA_real_, 0L))
    c(mean(target[ok] >= lo[ok] & target[ok] <= hi[ok]), sum(ok))
  }
  .cov1_n <- function(target, b1, side = "lower") {   # one-sided: target >= lower bound,
    target <- rep_len(target, length(b1))               # or target <= upper bound
    ok <- is.finite(target) & is.finite(b1)
    if (!any(ok)) return(c(NA_real_, 0L))
    c(if (identical(side, "upper")) mean(target[ok] <= b1[ok])
      else mean(target[ok] >= b1[ok]), sum(ok))
  }
  z95 <- qnorm(0.95)

  cov_rows <- function(suffix, tgt_cde, tgt_marg) {
    keys <- est_keys_for(rF, suffix)
    or_est <- rF[[paste0("or_", suffix, "_est")]]
    bH_est <- rF[[paste0("betaHhat_", suffix)]]
    tgt <- list(oracle = or_est, betaHhat = bH_est, cde = tgt_cde, marg = tgt_marg)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(keys), function(lab) {
      k  <- keys[[lab]]
      ec <- .est_cols(rF, k, suffix)
      # One-sided 95% bound, on the block's exposed side: the harm block's
      # LOWER bound (harm claim), the complement's UPPER bound (benefit claim
      # "at most U"; TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06).  The field stores
      # its own (lambda q95 / q05 inversion); the normal-based estimators
      # derive exp(log est -/+ z95 * se_beta) -- the same construction as
      # their two-sided bounds, so this is a convention, not a new model.
      side <- if (identical(suffix, "Hc")) "upper" else "lower"
      sgn  <- if (identical(side, "upper")) 1 else -1
      b1 <- if (k == "fld") rF[[paste0("fld_", suffix, if (side == "upper") "_up1s" else "_lo1s")]]
            else { seb <- .get_se(rF, k, suffix)
                   ifelse(is.finite(ec$e) & is.finite(seb) & ec$e > 0,
                          exp(log(ec$e) + sgn * z95 * seb), NA_real_) }
      do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tgt), function(tn) {
        c2 <- .cov_n(tgt[[tn]], ec$lo, ec$hi)
        w  <- .wilson(c2[1], c2[2])
        c1 <- .cov1_n(tgt[[tn]], b1, side)
        data.frame(Block = if (suffix == "H") "Harm Ĥ" else "Complement Ĥᶜ",
                   Estimator = lab, Target = tn,
                   n = as.integer(c2[2]), Cov2s = c2[1],
                   W_lo = w[1], W_hi = w[2], Cov1s = c1[1], Side = side,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }))
    }))
  }
  cw <- rbind(cov_rows("H",  truth$cde_H,  truth$marg_H),
              cov_rows("Hc", truth$cde_Hc, truth$marg_Hc))
  gt(cw, groupname_col = "Block") |>
    tab_header(title = "95% coverage with Wilson intervals (two-sided primary; one-sided supplementary)",
               subtitle = "Targets: per-replicate oracle; beta(Hhat) (conditional, primary); CDE; marginal") |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(Cov2s, W_lo, W_hi, Cov1s), decimals = 3) |>
    cols_label(Cov2s = "2-sided cov", W_lo = "Wilson lo", W_hi = "Wilson hi",
               Cov1s = "1-sided cov", Side = "1-sided bound") |>
    tab_footnote(footnote = md(paste(
      "Wilson interval on the two-sided coverage proportion (paper convention, primary; F4).",
      "One-sided coverage on the block's exposed side -- harm block: share of replicates with target >= the 95% LOWER bound;",
      "complement block: share with target <= the 95% UPPER bound (benefit claim; TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06).",
      "The field rows use their stored `lower_1s` / `upper_1s` (lambda q95 / q05 inversion); the normal-based rows use exp(log est -/+ 1.645 se).")))
}

# Complement field block (field_complement = TRUE renders only;
# TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06).  Retained bias of naive / MR (IJ) /
# MR (field) est2 against beta(Hhat^c), the complement's lambda-SD/SD and

if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && "fld_Hc_est2" %in% names(results) &&
    any(is.finite(results$fld_Hc_est2))) {
  rC <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  okc <- is.finite(rC$betaHhat_Hc) & rC$betaHhat_Hc > 0
  .retc <- function(est) {
    d <- log(est[okc]) - log(rC$betaHhat_Hc[okc]); d <- d[is.finite(d)]
    c(mean = mean(d), sd_est = stats::sd(d), n = length(d))
  }
  rbc_nv  <- .retc(rC$nv_Hc_est)
  rbc_mr  <- .retc(rC$mr_Hc_est)
  rbc_fld <- .retc(rC$fld_Hc_est2)
  sdc_fld <- .sd_log(rC$fld_Hc_est2)
  sdc_mr  <- .sd_log(rC$mr_Hc_est)
  lamc_ratio <- .mfin(rC$fld_Hc_se) / sdc_fld
  ijc_ratio  <- .mfin(rC$mr_Hc_se_ij) / sdc_mr
  # One-sided upper margin (log scale): field = log up1s - log(mr_Hc_est)
  # (the field inverts about beta-tilde^c); IJ = 1.645 * se_ij.
  marg_fld <- .mfin(log(rC$fld_Hc_up1s) - log(rC$mr_Hc_est))
  marg_ij  <- .mfin(qnorm(0.95) * rC$mr_Hc_se_ij)
  hw_fld   <- .mfin((log(rC$fld_Hc_hi2s) - log(rC$fld_Hc_lo2s)) / 2)
  hw_ij    <- .mfin((log(rC$mr_Hc_hi) - log(rC$mr_Hc_lo)) / 2)
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(
    quantity = c("naive retained bias vs beta(Hhat^c)  [log-HR]",

Code 
# Simultaneous (H lower, Hc upper) pair (TASK_complement_refinements_2026-09-06,
# method B; field_complement = TRUE renders only).  Joint coverage
# beta(Hhat) >= lower_H  AND  beta(Hhat^c) <= upper_Hc for (i) the two separate
# 95% field bounds, (ii) the Bonferroni pair, (iii) the calibrated pair;
# the two margins (log scale) for each; mean gamma, achieved joint probability
# and the draws' correlation.
if (run_smoke && !is.null(results) && "fld_joint_gamma" %in% names(results) &&
    any(is.finite(results$fld_joint_gamma))) {
  rJ <- results[results$detected == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  okj <- is.finite(rJ$betaHhat_H) & is.finite(rJ$betaHhat_Hc) & is.finite(rJ$fld_joint_gamma)
  rJ <- rJ[okj, , drop = FALSE]
  .wl <- function(x, n, z = qnorm(0.975)) {
    ctr <- (x + z^2/(2*n))/(1 + z^2/n); hw <- z*sqrt(x*(1-x)/n + z^2/(4*n^2))/(1 + z^2/n)
    sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", x, ctr - hw, ctr + hw)
  }
  pairs <- list(
    `separate 95% field bounds` = list(lo = rJ$fld_H_lo1s, up = rJ$fld_Hc_up1s),
    `Bonferroni (gamma = 0.025)` = list(lo = rJ$fld_joint_bonf_loH, up = rJ$fld_joint_bonf_upHc),
    `calibrated gamma`           = list(lo = rJ$fld_joint_loH, up = rJ$fld_joint_upHc))
  jt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pairs), function(nm) {
    p <- pairs[[nm]]
    covH  <- rJ$betaHhat_H >= p$lo; covC <- rJ$betaHhat_Hc <= p$up
    data.frame(pair = nm, n = nrow(rJ),
               joint_cov = .wl(mean(covH & covC), nrow(rJ)),
               cov_H = mean(covH), cov_Hc = mean(covC),
               margin_H = mean(log(rJ$mr_H_est) - log(p$lo)),
               margin_Hc = mean(log(p$up) - log(rJ$mr_Hc_est)),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  print(knitr::kable(jt, digits = 3,
    caption = sprintf("Joint (Hhat lower, Hhat^c upper) coverage of (beta(Hhat), beta(Hhat^c)) with Wilson intervals; margins on the log scale from the two-term de-biased estimates. Mean gamma = %.4f (achieved joint prob. %.3f; Bonferroni %.3f); mean corr(Lambda*, Lambda*c) = %+.3f; n_joint_draws mean %.0f.",
                      mean(rJ$fld_joint_gamma), mean(rJ$fld_joint_prob), mean(rJ$fld_joint_bonf_prob),
                      mean(rJ$fld_joint_corr), mean(rJ$fld_joint_n))))
}

16 Identification structure

The supplement’s identification summary (its Figures/Table “FS identification structure”), computed here on this run rather than assembled separately. The engine is fs_identification_summary() in the package, so this document, the continuous twin, and the manuscript fragments all share one implementation.

Each detected replicate’s realized rule is classified against the planted triple: the anchor er, its true binary partner meno, and the correlated continuous proxy age that may substitute for the partner. The near-tie between \(\{\mathrm{er} \cap \mathrm{meno}\}\) and its age proxy is the phenomenon these summaries exist to expose.

# Sweep points are supplied as a NAMED list; a single batch has one point.  The
# manuscript figures pass two or more (n = 500, 1000, ...) and the same call
# draws the trend.  Bundles may be given as in-memory frames (as here) or as
# paths to saved .rds files.
#
# Classification keys on `sg_def`, so this works whether or not `covs` was
# populated -- the GLM/continuous harness leaves `covs` empty by design, and
# reading it directly would classify every replicate as "anchor missed".
id_run <- fs_identification_summary(
  bundles = stats::setNames(list(results), as.character(n_sample)),
  anchor  = "er",     # the factor FS recovers as the trial grows
  partner = "meno",   # the true binary partner
  proxy   = "age",    # correlated continuous covariate FS may substitute
  confounders = confounders_base,
  sweep_label = "Trial size (n)")

# PORTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN.  Complementary to the structure summary
# above: that classifies each rule into five categories, this shows the raw
# per-covariate selection shares over the whole analysis pool, plus the realized
# rules by frequency.
if (nrow(.rI)) {
  .cov_list <- lapply(.rI$sg_def, rule_covs)
  .cov_all  <- unique(unlist(.cov_list))
  if (length(.cov_all)) {
    .cf <- vapply(.cov_all, function(v)
      mean(vapply(.cov_list, function(x) v %in% x, logical(1))), numeric(1))
    .cf_df <- data.frame(covariate = names(.cf), share = unname(.cf))
    .cf_df$true_region <- .cf_df$covariate %in% c("er", "meno")
    print(
      ggplot(.cf_df, aes(x = reorder(covariate, share), y = share, fill = true_region)) +
        geom_col() + coord_flip() +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "firebrick", `FALSE` = "grey60"),
                          labels = c(`TRUE` = "true-region covariate", `FALSE` = "other"),
                          name = NULL) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of detected replicates selecting the covariate",
             title = "Selected-covariate frequencies",
             subtitle = "True harm region: er <= 8 & meno == 0") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
    # COLLAPSED OVER CUT VALUES.  The raw rules-by-frequency table listed every
    # distinct `sg_def` string and was dominated by cut noise -- on a
    # 500-replicate survival run, 322 distinct rules over 346 detections, with
    # `{age <= 46} & {nodes <= 5}` and `{nodes <= 3} & {age <= 46}` as separate
    # rows despite being the same pairing.  fs_rule_covariate_pairs() sorts and
    # de-duplicates the covariate names, so orderings collapse together, as do
    # equivalent spellings of one condition (`!{meno}` vs `{meno == 0}`).  The
    # same run reduces to 22 signatures.
    #
    # `k` is the number of DISTINCT covariates, so a band on a single variable
    # (`!{nodes <= 3} & {nodes <= 5}`) shows as k = 1 rather than being hidden;
    # `n_rules` is how many distinct rule strings collapsed into the row.
    .pairs <- fs_rule_covariate_pairs(.rI, true_covariates = c("er", "meno"))
    print(plot_fs_rule_pairs(.rI, true_covariates = c("er", "meno"), top_n = 12L))
    knitr::kable(.pairs, digits = 3,
      caption = paste("Selected-covariate-pair frequencies: realized rules",
                      "collapsed over cut values, detected reps.",
                      "`k` = distinct covariates in the signature;",
                      "`n_rules` = distinct rule strings that collapsed into it."))
  }

  • Target semantics to confirm. The three targets here are (per-replicate oracle, DGM cde_H/cde_Hc, DGM hr_H_true/hr_Hc_true). Before publishing numbers, confirm these match the \(\theta^{\ddagger}\)/\(\theta^{\dagger}\) definitions used by build_estimation_table() / León Table 5.

# Single, unambiguous start-to-finish wall-clock: from the first line of `setup`
# to here.  This is the true total cost of running the whole document -- setup +
# library loads + DGM build + every simulation replicate (MR AND FB
# bootstrap) + all table rendering -- not a per-rep mean or a model.
.fmt_dur <- function(s) {
  h <- s %/% 3600; m <- (s %% 3600) %/% 60; sec <- round(s %% 60)
  if (h >= 1) sprintf("%d h %02d m %02d s", h, m, sec)
  else if (m >= 1) sprintf("%d m %02d s", m, sec)
  else sprintf("%.1f s", s)
}
.secs_total <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .t0_doc, units = "secs"))
cat(sprintf("TOTAL wall-clock, start to finish: %s  (= %.0f s; %d reps on %d workers)\n",
            .fmt_dur(.secs_total), .secs_total, n_sims, n_workers))

> **Status — combined FB / MR (IJ) / MR (field) template**
> (`TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05`). Derived from the committed
> `sim_fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_m1_h10_knoise0_n500_batch_1_1000.qmd` with knob
> deltas only: `ci_method = "field"` (the debiased element keeps the IJ
> interval, so the MR (IJ) columns are unchanged; the field block is recorded
> alongside), an `fb_mode` knob (`"run"` computes FB in-replicate; `"join"`
> reads a committed FB bundle and joins by `sim_id`, never recomputing FB;
> `"none"` skips it), and a `campaign_tag` in the output stem so this template
> can never write into an existing stem (the h-tag is also widened to three
> digits, `h100`/`h175`, closing the `round(10*1.75) = round(10*1.8) = 18`
> collision). Every knob can be overridden per render through `FS_S7_*`
> environment variables (see @sec-setup), so batches run from ONE committed
> file. `run_mode` and `sim_id_start` split a long run into seed-disjoint
> batches that combine later; `run_mode = "combine"` renders every table on
> the pooled set. `FS_S7_FIELD_COMPLEMENT` adds the complement's
> field block (`fld_Hc_*`, one-sided **upper** bound primary;
> `TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06`) and `FS_S7_FIELD_SCALEC` selects its
> studentized companion (field-s). Both default to the recommended
> constructions as of `TASK_cert20_2026-09-08` Part D (`TRUE` / `selected`);
> `FALSE` / `none` restore the prior behaviour, in which case the bundle is
> byte-identical to a pre-complement render.

# What this evaluates {#sec-intro}

**Multiplier resampling (MR)** (`fs_mr_inference()`, surfaced through
`forestsearch(mr_inference = TRUE)`) is a refit-free multiplier-bootstrap
approximation of León's post-selection bias correction, with an
infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) confidence interval. To first order its point
estimate equals León's Eq. 7 correction and its interval equals León's IJ
variance, the only approximation being the per-subgroup `dfbeta` linearization.

This document turns the single-trial validation into operating characteristics by
re-running the León (2024) estimation/coverage design and recording, **per
replicate on the same data and the same selected subgroup**:

* **oracle** $\hat\theta(H)$ — refit on the *true* harm subgroup;
* **naive** $\hat\theta(\hat H)$ — plugin on the identified subgroup;
* **FB** $\hat\theta^{*}(\hat H)$ — full nonparametric bootstrap
  bias-correction (`forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()`, León Eq. 7, the `H2`
  variant accounting for both bias sources) with its IJ interval;
* **MR** $\tilde\theta(\hat H)$ — refit-free multiplier resampling, holding the
  fitted candidate family fixed, with its IJ interval.

Each is compared to three truth targets: the per-replicate **oracle** estimate,
the controlled direct effect $\theta^{\ddagger}$ (CDE), and the marginal subgroup
hazard ratio $\theta^{\dagger}$. The two outputs are (1) the León Table-2-layout
estimation/coverage table with an MR block, and (2) the paired
FB$\leftrightarrow$MR agreement panel.  For `consistency` (a fixed
candidate family) that panel is the most direct empirical check of the
leading-order correspondence; for `dina`/`grf` the bootstrap regenerates the
family per resample, so the panel instead measures the family-regeneration gap
between the unconditional (FB) and conditional-on-family (MR) estimands.

The search runs under `consistency_method = "resample"` and
`sg_focus = "maxcons"` — the consistency argmax: highest consistency rate,
ties broken by effect. MR de-biases against that same candidate family, using
the rule `forestsearch()` derives from `sg_focus` rather than one set here, so
FB and MR share the same selection map. MR does not identify a subgroup; the
one reported is the one the search selected.

# The true subgroup {#sec-truth}

Everything below is scored against one planted region, so it is stated first.

**Definition.** $Q = \{\mathrm{er} \le 8\} \cap \{\mathrm{meno} = 0\}$ --- low
estrogen receptor **and** premenopausal. The `er` threshold is the 25th
percentile of the GBSG covariate template (er ranges 0--1144, median 36); the
`meno` term is the raw binary. The region covers **12.2%** of the template
(84 of 686 patients), and the DGM plants the harm effect there via
`setup_gbsg_dgm()`, which encodes it as `z1 = 1 & z3 = 1`.

**Why this region.** GBSG is a node-positive breast-cancer cohort, and
`er`/`meno` are the two covariates that jointly define endocrine
responsiveness: hormone-receptor status and menopausal status are the standard
axes on which adjuvant endocrine benefit is expected to differ. Planting harm
in the ER-low, premenopausal corner therefore makes the target clinically
coherent rather than an arbitrary covariate pair, and its ~12% prevalence puts
it in the small-subgroup regime that stresses the large-sample behaviour of the
correction --- which is the point of the exercise.

**What the search must do.** The analysis pool is the RAW covariates
(`er, age, meno, pgr, nodes, size, grade`); the pre-dichotomised `z1..z5` are
never supplied. The search has to rediscover both the variable pair and the
cut. `conf.cont_jcuts = list(er = 10)` deliberately replaces `er`'s default
cuts with a J-quantile grid at the $k/(J+1)$ quantiles --- `0, 3, 9, 17, 30,
44, 69.8, 100, 173.5, 293.7` --- which does **not** contain 8. The exact
boundary is therefore not on the grid and must be approximated. That is
deliberate: a design in which the true cut is a candidate hands the search the
answer.

**The near-tie this creates.** `age` correlates with `meno` strongly enough to
substitute for it, so the search can return $\{\mathrm{er}\} \cap
\{\mathrm{age}\}$ in place of $\{\mathrm{er}\} \cap \{\mathrm{meno}\}$ at
nearly equal fit. @sec-identification quantifies how often it does, and whether
more data resolves it.

# Endpoints, subgroups, and the harm convention {#sec-definitions}

**Endpoint.** `simulate_from_dgm()` emits a time-to-event pair: `y_sim` (the
event or censoring time, months) with indicator `event_sim`. Survival times come
from the AFT model fitted to the GBSG covariate template; censoring is Weibull,
scaled by `cens_adjust = log(1.5)`, with administrative censoring at
`analysis_time = 84` months. Treatment is `treat_sim`, randomised 1:1.

**Effect measure.** The Cox hazard ratio of treatment, estimated within a
region by `coxph(Surv(y_sim, event_sim) ~ treat_sim)`. Model SEs
(`*_se` columns) are on the **log**-hazard-ratio scale while point estimates
and interval bounds are on the **HR** scale; the estimation table reports
$\text{SD}_{\beta}$ and $\widehat{\text{SD}}_{\beta}$ on the log scale and
hides the HR-scale twins.

**Harm.** On a hazard ratio, larger is worse: $\text{HR} > 1$ means treatment
raises the hazard, so **harm is HR > 1** and the null is HR = 1. Nothing is
re-oriented on this path --- every estimator column, every interval bound, and
every target is on the natural HR scale as fitted. (The continuous twin *does*
re-orient, because its raw scale runs the other way; see its matching section.)

**The three regions.**

* $Q$ --- the **true** planted region, $\{\mathrm{er} \le 8\} \cap
  \{\mathrm{meno} = 0\}$, known to the DGM and carried per subject as
  `flag_harm`. Fixed across replicates. Defined and motivated in @sec-truth.
* $\widehat H$ --- the **realized** region: whatever rule the search returned on
  this replicate, recorded as `sg_def`. Varies replicate to replicate, and is
  the region the naive, FB and MR estimators are computed on. Membership is
  `treat.recommend == 0`.
* $\widehat H^{c}$ --- its complement within the trial, `treat.recommend == 1`.

The **oracle** is the only estimator fitted on $Q$; naive, FB and MR are all
fitted on $\widehat H$. That is why the oracle's meaningful comparisons are
against the true-region targets and not against $\beta(\widehat H)$.

**The four targets** each estimator is scored against, in the notation the
estimation table uses: $\hat\theta(H)$ the per-replicate oracle; $\beta(\widehat
H)$ the population effect at the *realized* region (the Theorem 2 target, and
the only one that moves with $\widehat H$); $\theta^{\ddagger}$ the CDE at $Q$;
and $\theta^{\dagger}$ the marginal effect at $Q$. The last two differ here
because the hazard ratio is non-collapsible.

## How "MR flags harm in x%" is computed {#sec-mr-harm}

The estimation-table footnote reports the share of replicates in which MR
**confirms** harm. That is a decision, not an estimate, and it is separate from
the interval: it asks whether the *de-biased* effect still points at harm after
the selection correction, which is exactly the question the naive estimate
cannot answer.

**The rule.** `fs_mr_inference()` de-biases the naive subgroup effect, then
applies one comparison on the working scale
(`fs_mr_inference.R`):

```
t_cmp    <- if (log_scale) log(t_confirm) else t_confirm
ci_lo_1s <- beta_deb - qnorm(0.95) * se
flag     <- if (confirm_rule == "point") (beta_deb >= t_cmp)
            else                          (ci_lo_1s >= t_cmp)
```

`beta_deb` is the de-biased estimate and `se` the interval SE (the IJ SE under
`ci_method = "ij"`). So `"point"` asks whether the de-biased **point estimate**
clears the threshold, and `"ci"` asks whether the one-sided 95%
selection-adjusted **lower bound** does --- strictly the more conservative of
the two. The result is `harm_flag`, surfaced on the fitted object as
`mr_harm_confirmed` and recorded here as `mr_harm_flag`.

**The threshold, and why it sits at the null.** On this path the effect measure is the hazard ratio, so the working
scale is the **log** scale and `t_confirm` is compared as `log(t_confirm)`.
Leaving `mr_t_confirm = NULL` takes the package's near-null default,
`t_confirm = 1` for ratio measures, so by default the question is
"is the de-biased hazard ratio still at or above 1?" --- *not* whether it still clears the screening
threshold used during the search. That distinction is deliberate and
`fs_mr_inference()` documents the reason: the de-biasing correction over-shrinks
true effects, so testing against a screening-level threshold would reject
genuine subgroups. Raising it to, say, `mr_t_confirm <- 1.10` would demand a de-biased HR of
at least 1.10 before harm is called.

**Three-valued, and why that matters for the percentage.** `harm_flag` is
`TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NA`, the last when MR ran but bailed before it could
compute one. The package documentation is explicit that `NA` here is *absence
of evidence, not evidence against harm*, and warns against `isTRUE()`, which
collapses `NA` to `FALSE`. This document records the flag three-valued and the
reported percentage is `mean(..., na.rm = TRUE)`, so those replicates leave the
denominator rather than entering it as "harm not confirmed".

**Controlling it.** Both settings are knobs in @sec-setup --- `mr_t_confirm`
and `mr_confirm_rule` --- assembled into `mr_inference_args` and passed to
`forestsearch(mr_inference_args = ...)`. `mr_t_confirm` is on the **effect**
scale, not the working log scale; the code takes the log internally for ratio
measures. The settings actually used are echoed in @sec-counts, after the run, so what
is reported is what was used rather than what was intended.


# Setup — all knobs {#sec-setup}

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.t0_doc <- Sys.time()    # start of document-level wall-clock (total reported at the very end)

# NOTE: forestsearch must be INSTALLED (devtools::install()), not load_all():
# the doFuture multisession workers spawn separate R processes that only see the
# installed package.
library(forestsearch)
library(survival)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(foreach)
library(doFuture)
library(future)

# Parallelization topology (works with run_mode / batching above):
#   "sims"  -> replicates fan out across workers; each replicate's forestsearch +
#              bootstrap run sequentially.  Best when n_sims >= n_workers (fills cores).
#   "boots" -> replicates run sequentially; the forestsearch search AND the nb_boots
#              bootstrap fan out across workers WITHIN each replicate.  Best when
#              n_sims is small (single-/few-trial deep dives) and "sims" would idle cores.
# Bootstrap resample indices are seeded on the main process, so results are
# plan-invariant: the two modes differ in WALL-CLOCK only, not in detection/estimates.
parallel_mode <- "sims"

# ── Environment overrides (FS_S7_*) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# ONE committed file runs every batch: each knob below reads an FS_S7_* env var
# first and falls back to the in-file default, so an unattended driver renders
#   FS_S7_HR=1.75 FS_S7_START=1001 FS_S7_NSIMS=1000 FS_S7_FB=none \
#     quarto render sim_fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_field_m1_template.qmd --output ...
# without ever editing the committed template.  Every resolved value is echoed
# below and lands in the bundle's meta, so a render is auditable from its
# output alone.
.env_chr <- function(k, d) { v <- Sys.getenv(k, unset = NA); if (is.na(v) || !nzchar(v)) d else v }
.env_int <- function(k, d) as.integer(.env_chr(k, d))
.env_num <- function(k, d) as.numeric(.env_chr(k, d))

# ── Counts (the only knobs to change for production) ───────────────────────
n_sims       <- .env_int("FS_S7_NSIMS", 1000L)   # simulated trials per batch
diag_mode    <- FALSE     # DIAGNOSTIC: TRUE caps the run to 5 replicates and relays each
                          # worker's forestsearch() error (otherwise swallowed by the inner
                          # tryCatch).  Set FALSE for a real run.
# fb_mode governs the FB comparator (decision F5 of the task):
#   "run"  -> compute FB in-replicate (nb_boots below must be >= 1)
#   "join" -> NEVER recompute FB: read the committed FB bundle at fb_join_path
#             and join its fb_* columns by sim_id after the run loop.  sim_ids
#             outside the bundle simply stay NA (recorded as FB-absent).
#   "none" -> no FB at all.
fb_mode      <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FB", "none")     # "run" | "join" | "none"
stopifnot(fb_mode %in% c("run", "join", "none"))
fb_join_path <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FB_PATH",
  "results/fs_maxeffCons_fb_mr_m1_h10_knoise0_n500_combined_1_500.rds")
# GATE 2 AMENDMENT (Larry, 2026-09-05, Stage 2 STOP resolution -- the
# authorized one-knob change): enumerated cross-vintage selection-flip
# replicates.  The committed h10 bundles (forestsearch 0.2.0/0.2.1) and the
# current package (0.3.5) select a different near-tie rule on exactly these
# sim_ids (REPORT_mr_field_s7_stage2_2026-09-05.md: sims 393, 780; data and
# oracle identical, selection flips at the consistency screen).  The FB-join
# identity assertion still STOPS on any replicate NOT in this list; listed
# replicates are skipped -- never joined, recorded FB-absent -- with both
# selections (committed and fresh) printed.  Recorded in meta.  h175 has no
# flips; the list is inert there (fb_mode is never "join" for h175).
fb_join_skip <- local({
  v <- .env_chr("FS_S7_JOIN_SKIP", "393,780")
  if (nzchar(v)) sort(unique(as.integer(strsplit(v, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))) else integer(0)
})
nb_boots     <- if (identical(fb_mode, "run")) .env_int("FS_S7_NB_BOOTS", 300L) else 0L
k_random_noise <- .env_int("FS_S7_KNOISE", 0L)   # Add k_random_noise confounders

# ── Batching across renders (split one long run into seed-disjoint pieces) ──
# Each render is ONE batch of `n_sims` replicates starting at `sim_id_start`.
# Every per-replicate seed is `seed_base + sim_id` (DGM, search, bootstrap, AND
# the noise covariates), so disjoint sim_id ranges across renders are independent
# and pool to exactly what one big run would have produced:
#
#   Batch 1 : run_mode "batch", sim_id_start = 1     -> ..._res_1_100.rds
#   Batch 2 : run_mode "batch", sim_id_start = 101   -> ..._res_101_200.rds   (re-render)
#   ...      (re-render per batch, advancing sim_id_start by n_sims each time)
#   Combine : run_mode "combine"                     -> reads ..._res_*.rds, rbinds,
#                                                       renders every table on the union
#
# DEFAULT is a single batch starting at 1: render once and you have the whole run.
run_mode     <- .env_chr("FS_S7_MODE", "batch")   # "batch" (run + save one piece) | "combine" (merge + report)
sim_id_start <- .env_int("FS_S7_START", 1L)       # first sim_id of THIS batch (1001L, ... for later pieces)

# ── The identifier: engine + focus ─────────────────────────────────────────
# These two together ARE the estimator, and both feed the output stem below,
# so they are defined here rather than with the search-tuning knobs.  Defining
# sg_focus later would leave focus_tag undefined at stem-construction time.
# ENGINE KNOB (FS_S7_METHOD; TASK_dinamr_campaign_2026-09-10 Part T).  The value
# was a hard-coded literal here, so a DINA or GRF campaign meant duplicating the
# whole template.  Reading it from the environment is document-level, add-only
# and default-inert: with FS_S7_METHOD unset it resolves to "consistency" --
# exactly the former literal -- so every committed consistency campaign renders
# unchanged.  method_tag, focus_tag and the output stem already key on it just
# below, so a run under a different engine can never overwrite a consistency
# bundle, and meta$subgroup_method (already written in both the batch and the
# combined bundle, and already in combine mode's poolability key vector)
# records which engine produced a file.
subgroup_method <- .env_chr("FS_S7_METHOD", "consistency")  # "consistency" | "dina" | "grf"
stopifnot(subgroup_method %in% c("consistency", "dina", "grf"))
# Identifier focus knob (TASK_p30_effMaxSG_2026-09-06): "maxeffCons" (the
# consistency-screened effect argmax; every committed campaign) or "effMaxSG"
# (the largest subgroup within effect_neighborhood = 0.10 of the maximal
# effect among the same screened candidates).  forestsearch() derives MR's
# re-selection rule from sg_focus, so the gate re-selects under the same
# functional (REPORT_p30sg_stage0); the stem follows focus_tag as it always has.
sg_focus           <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FOCUS", "maxeffCons")
# "maxSG" / "minSG" (TASK_complement_variance_banddial_2026-09-07, Part B): the
# pure size rules over the same consistency-qualifying candidates -- the
# identifier sorts (-N, -Pcons, K) / (N, -Pcons, K), the gate re-selects
# which.max / which.min of size among the passers (the aligned maps quoted at
# nb20 Stage 0 0d and re-confirmed at banddial Stage 0).  effect_neighborhood
# is inert under both (band_n below is then the eps-band on the observed
# effects, recorded for information only).  Guard widened; nothing else keys
# on the value.
# Part B (TASK_partB_enabling_2026-09-12, 1b): widened to the six Part B
# criteria.  "effMinSG" is the band rule's smallest-subgroup arm; "maxeff" is
# the unconditional effect argmax on the consistency engine (it disables the
# consistency and effect floors, forestsearch_main.R:1537-1571) and, like
# "maxeffCons", resolves to the plain effect argmax on DINA and GRF
# (fs_focus_tag.R:76-86).  Still a guard: anything else stops the render.
stopifnot(sg_focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "maxeffCons", "effMinSG", "maxSG", "minSG", "maxeff"))
.band_foci <- c("effMaxSG", "effMinSG")
# Band-width and er-grid knobs (TASK_p30sg_nb20_2026-09-07; document-level,
# add-only, defaults reproduce p30sg exactly).  effect_neighborhood is the
# identifier's band half-width (hr >= (1 - eps) * max hr among the
# consistency-qualifying candidates; REPORT_p30sg_stage0 0a'), forwarded to
# the gate unchanged by forestsearch() as `nbhd`; er_jcuts is the J of the
# J-quantile grid on raw ER (conf.cont_jcuts = list(er = J)).  Both are read
# HERE, before the stem, because non-default values tag the stem below.
effect_neighborhood <- .env_num("FS_S7_NBHD", 0.10)
stopifnot(is.finite(effect_neighborhood), effect_neighborhood >= 0, effect_neighborhood < 1)
# Part B (1b): eps belongs to the band foci only.  Supplying FS_S7_NBHD with any
# other focus is an error, not a silently inert setting.  Unset, the 0.10
# default is still forwarded (it is forestsearch()'s own default, :1254), so
# every committed non-band render is unchanged.  The package itself only
# errors on a non-default selection_rule (.validate_selection_rule(),
# R/subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:743); this eps check is template policy.
if (!sg_focus %in% .band_foci && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FS_S7_NBHD")))
  stop(sprintf("FS_S7_NBHD is set (%s) but sg_focus = '%s' does not consult effect_neighborhood; it is accepted only for %s.",
               Sys.getenv("FS_S7_NBHD"), sg_focus, paste(.band_foci, collapse = " / ")),
       call. = FALSE)
er_jcuts            <- .env_int("FS_S7_ER_JCUTS", 10L)
stopifnot(is.finite(er_jcuts), er_jcuts >= 1L)

target_hr_harm  <- .env_num("FS_S7_HR", 1.0)   # calibrate k_inter to this Cox HR in the harm subgroup
n_sample        <- .env_int("FS_S7_N", 500L)   # M1 sample size
# ── Harm-subgroup prevalence knob (TASK_prevalence30_2026-09-06) ─────────────
# z1_quantile is the engine's own formal: the harm rule is
#   {er <= quantile(er, z1_quantile)} & {meno == 0}
# (the same form at every value).  0.25 is M1 (er <= 8, prevalence 12.4%) and
# the package default, so a render without FS_S7_Z1Q is byte-identical to the
# committed s7/s7c/map1/map1c bundles; 0.60 is the ~30% cell (er <= 59,
# prevalence 0.3065 on the super-population).  Passed to BOTH the calibration
# and the DGM build, so k_inter is calibrated under the same rule it plants.
# Caution recorded at Gate 0: at 0.60 the 30% region is planted rather than
# data-supported (the GBSG-fitted zh interaction is ~0 there), with effective
# interaction sizes comparable to M1's.
harm_z1_quantile <- .env_num("FS_S7_Z1Q", 0.25)
stopifnot(harm_z1_quantile > 0, harm_z1_quantile < 1)
# -- Structural-null DGM switch (TASK_null_gbsg_identification_2026-09-21) ----
# dgm_model was the literal "alt" at the DGM block below.  FS_S7_DGM reads it
# from the environment: unset (or "alt") reproduces the former literal exactly,
# so every committed render is unchanged.
#
#   "alt"  : the planted-region design.  {er <= quantile(er, z1_quantile) &
#            meno == 0} carries the zh interaction; FS_S7_HR calibrates k_inter
#            to the Cox HR inside that region (calibrate_k_inter, k_treat = 1).
#   "null" : the STRUCTURAL null.  .create_gbsg_dgm_() drops zh from the design
#            entirely and sets flag.harm == 0 with fs_harm_true = NULL
#            (R/sim_aft_gbsg.R:302-310, :336-349, :370-378), so no region is
#            planted and every subject carries the same treatment effect
#            loghr_po = b0["treat"].  FS_S7_HR is then the target SUPER-
#            POPULATION MARGINAL Cox HR (dgm$hr_causal -- the same construction
#            that gives the alt design's complement effect hr_Hc_true), reached
#            by calibrating k_treat at the template level (calibrate_k_inter
#            refuses model != "alt", R/sim_aft_gbsg.R:1017-1020).
dgm_model <- .env_chr("FS_S7_DGM", "alt")
stopifnot(dgm_model %in% c("alt", "null"))
# The region rule is what z1_quantile parameterizes, and under "null" there is
# no region, so the knob would silently move the z1 MAIN effect alone.
# Rejected rather than left inert: the null cells must differ in the uniform
# effect only.  z1_quantile keeps its 0.25 default (the M1 value) on both.
if (identical(dgm_model, "null") && nzchar(Sys.getenv("FS_S7_Z1Q")))
  stop(sprintf("FS_S7_Z1Q is set (%s) but FS_S7_DGM = 'null' plants no region; the quantile would move the z1 main effect only.",
               Sys.getenv("FS_S7_Z1Q")), call. = FALSE)
# ── MR switch (TASK_partB_enabling_2026-09-12, 1a) ───────────────────────────
# forestsearch(mr_inference = ...) was a literal TRUE.  FS_S7_MR reads it from
# the environment: unset (or TRUE) reproduces the former literal exactly, so
# every committed render is unchanged; FALSE runs identification and
# classification only.  MR cannot change the identified subgroup
# (R/forestsearch_main.R:1041-1044).  Read HERE because FALSE tags the stem.
mr_inference_on <- .env_chr("FS_S7_MR", "TRUE")
stopifnot(mr_inference_on %in% c("TRUE", "FALSE"))
mr_inference_on <- identical(mr_inference_on, "TRUE")
# Winner-only / winner-floor IJ rows (TASK_complement_refinements): rejected
# on theoretical grounds and not evaluated going forward; excluded from every
# table and figure unless FS_S7_WINNER_ROWS=TRUE (the recorder columns stay).
show_winner_rows <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_WINNER_ROWS", "FALSE"), "TRUE")

# Output stem derives from the knobs above, so changing n_sample / target_hr_harm /
# k_random_noise / subgroup_method / sg_focus renames every saved file automatically
# -- no manual edit, and runs under a different engine or focus never overwrite each
# other. The leading token IS the subgroup method: "fs" for consistency, else
# "dina"/"grf"; focus_tag follows it. Batch range is appended below.
#
# NOT back-compatible: the stem changed from "<engine>_t1_t2_m1_..." to
# "<engine>_<focus>_fb_mr_m1_...".  Batch .rds files written under the old stem
# are invisible to combine_glob -- re-run them or rename them to match.
method_tag   <- if (identical(subgroup_method, "consistency")) "fs" else subgroup_method

# The IDENTIFIER is the estimator here; FB and MR are resampling procedures applied
# to it.  The identifier has two parts -- the engine (method_tag) and the selection
# focus -- and only the engine was in the stem, so re-running a cell under a
# different sg_focus silently overwrote the same .rds, and combine_glob pooled the
# two together.  focus_tag closes that.
#
# Aliases normalize FORWARD to the descriptive name rather than back through
# .normalize_sg_focus(), which maps eff -> "hr": the Cox-flavoured internal
# vocabulary.  "eff*" generalizes across GLM outcomes, "hr" does not.
# Fold every alias pair onto one tag.  .normalize_sg_focus() collapses three
# pairs -- eff/hr, effMaxSG/hrMaxSG, effMinSG/hrMinSG -- so each pair is one
# rule under two spellings.  Without folding, identical runs written under
# different spellings land in different stems and never pool.  The eff*
# spelling wins because it carries over to GLM outcomes; the consistency
# argmax takes "maxcons", which names what the rule does.
# One source of truth: fs_focus_tag() holds the (subgroup_method, sg_focus)
# -> stem tag map for every driver.  It was pasted into each one and drifted;
# the method-blind copies tagged DINA/GRF runs with the consistency name for a
# rule those engines never ran.
focus_tag <- forestsearch::fs_focus_tag(subgroup_method, sg_focus)
if (!identical(focus_tag, sg_focus))
  cat(sprintf("NOTE: sg_focus '%s' is an alias on the %s path; output stem uses focus tag '%s'.
",
              sg_focus, subgroup_method, focus_tag))

# TEMPLATE STEM (three deliberate departures from the parent document, all
# collision guards per Gate 0 finding 2 of TASK_mr_field_section7_2026-09-05):
#   1. the token is "fb_mr_field", so no template output can ever glob-match
#      the committed fb_mr / mr stems;
#   2. the h-tag is THREE digits from round(100 * hr) -- h100, h175 -- closing
#      the parent's round(10*1.75) = round(10*1.8) = "h18" collision;
#   3. a mandatory campaign_tag suffix namespaces every campaign (smoke vs
#      production vs any rerun), so combine_glob can never pool across them.
campaign_tag <- .env_chr("FS_S7_CAMPAIGN", "c1")
# Alphanumerics and underscores (TASK_complement_variance_banddial_2026-09-07,
# C2, decision T-3): the tag is the stem's final token and combine_glob is
# "<stem>_res_*", so an underscore inside the tag cannot make one campaign's
# glob match another's.  Every committed tag (s7, s7c, map1, p30, p30sg,
# p30sgnb20, p30sgnb20j20, ...) is alphanumeric and unchanged.
stopifnot(grepl("^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$", campaign_tag))
# Prevalence tag only when the knob is non-default, so every committed M1 stem
# is unchanged (TASK_prevalence30_2026-09-06).
z1q_tag      <- if (abs(harm_z1_quantile - 0.25) < 1e-12) "" else
                  sprintf("_z1q%02d", round(100 * harm_z1_quantile))
# Structural-null tag (TASK_null_gbsg_identification_2026-09-21).  Empty under
# "alt", so every committed stem is unchanged.  It carries the target HR to
# THREE decimals because the h-tag above rounds to two (0.657 -> h066), and a
# null bundle must never share a stem -- or a combine_glob -- with an alt one.
dgm_tag      <- if (identical(dgm_model, "alt")) "" else
                  sprintf("_null%03d", round(1000 * target_hr_harm))
# Band / grid tags only when non-default, so every committed stem (p30sg
# included) is unchanged (TASK_p30sg_nb20_2026-09-07).
nbhd_tag     <- if (abs(effect_neighborhood - 0.10) < 1e-12) "" else
                  sprintf("_nb%02d", round(100 * effect_neighborhood))
jcuts_tag    <- if (er_jcuts == 10L) "" else sprintf("_j%d", er_jcuts)
# MR tag only when MR is off (Part B), so an identification-only bundle can
# never share a stem -- or a combine_glob -- with an MR bundle; every existing
# stem is unchanged.
mr_tag       <- if (isTRUE(mr_inference_on)) "" else "_nomr"
# Threshold knobs (TASK_null_gbsg_thresholds_2026-09-21_v2, Step 1).  FS_S7_C1
# and FS_S7_C2 set the screening threshold c1 (hr.threshold) and the per-split
# threshold c2 (hr.consistency) that the search chunk passes to forestsearch().
# Their defaults are the literals the search configuration carried before the
# knobs existed (0.90 / 0.80), so an unset render is unchanged.  Both or
# neither, and c2 <= c1.  p* stays the literal in the search configuration.
# They are read HERE, not there, because they tag the stem.
.c1_default <- 0.90
.c2_default <- 0.80
.c1_set <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("FS_S7_C1")); .c2_set <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("FS_S7_C2"))
if (xor(.c1_set, .c2_set))
  stop(sprintf("FS_S7_C1 and FS_S7_C2 must be set together (C1 '%s', C2 '%s').",
               Sys.getenv("FS_S7_C1"), Sys.getenv("FS_S7_C2")), call. = FALSE)
thr_c1 <- .env_num("FS_S7_C1", .c1_default)
thr_c2 <- .env_num("FS_S7_C2", .c2_default)
if (!is.finite(thr_c1) || !is.finite(thr_c2) || thr_c1 <= 0 || thr_c2 <= 0)
  stop(sprintf("FS_S7_C1 / FS_S7_C2 must be positive numbers (got %s / %s).",
               format(thr_c1), format(thr_c2)), call. = FALSE)
if (thr_c2 > thr_c1)
  stop(sprintf("FS_S7_C2 (%.4f) exceeds FS_S7_C1 (%.4f).", thr_c2, thr_c1), call. = FALSE)
# Threshold tag only when the pair differs from the defaults, so every
# committed stem is unchanged and a stricter-screen bundle can never share a
# stem -- or a combine_glob -- with one run at 0.90 / 0.80.
thr_tag      <- if (abs(thr_c1 - .c1_default) < 1e-12 && abs(thr_c2 - .c2_default) < 1e-12) "" else
                  sprintf("_c%03dc%03d", round(100 * thr_c1), round(100 * thr_c2))
rds_stem     <- sprintf("%s_%s_fb_mr_field_m1_h%03d_knoise%d_n%d%s%s%s%s%s%s_%s",
                        method_tag, focus_tag, round(100 * target_hr_harm),
                        k_random_noise, n_sample, dgm_tag, z1q_tag, nbhd_tag,
                        jcuts_tag, mr_tag, thr_tag, campaign_tag)

# ADOPTED FROM THE CONTINUOUS TWIN: quick-run stem tagging.
# Without this a smoke render (nb_boots = 10, n_sims = 20) writes to the SAME
# stem as a production batch, and combine_glob then pools the two silently --
# a handful of B = 10 replicates averaged in with B = 300 ones, with nothing in
# the pooled bundle recording that it happened.  Tagging the stem puts quick
# runs in a namespace combine can never match.  Set FALSE for production.
# (campaign_tag above already namespaces campaigns; quickrun is kept as a
# second, orthogonal guard for ad-hoc smoke renders inside a campaign.)
quickrun     <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_QUICKRUN", "FALSE"), "TRUE")
if (isTRUE(quickrun)) rds_stem <- paste0(rds_stem, "_quickrun")

sim_id_end   <- sim_id_start + n_sims - 1L
rds_path     <- file.path("results", sprintf("%s_res_%d_%d.rds", rds_stem, sim_id_start, sim_id_end))  # THIS batch's file
combine_glob <- file.path("results", sprintf("%s_res_*.rds", rds_stem))   # combine mode: which batch files to merge
combine_files <- NULL   # optional explicit character vector; NULL -> use combine_glob
# FS_S7_SAVE_COMBINED=FALSE lets a verification combine render run every
# table WITHOUT rewriting an already-committed pooled bundle (the committed
# bundles are read-only inputs; TASK_bias_coverage_display_2026-09-06).
save_combined <- !identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_SAVE_COMBINED", "TRUE"), "FALSE")   # combine mode: ALSO write the pooled bundle to disk
combined_path <- NULL   # NULL -> auto "results/<rds_stem>_combined_<min>_<max>.rds" (deliberately
                        # outside combine_glob, so a re-combine never re-ingests the pool)

# ── Persist results? The FB bootstrap (B x n_sims, each re-running the
# engine) is the wall-clock bottleneck; saving the results bundle lets you
# regenerate the summary tables without re-running the simulation. 

# Scale-up scenarios for the timing projection (n_sims, nb_boots). Edit freely.
proj_scenarios <- list(
  c(n_sims = 100L,  nb_boots = 300L),
  c(n_sims = 500L,  nb_boots = 300L),
  c(n_sims = 10000L, nb_boots = 500L)
)
                          # the MR -- see run_fb below.
mr_draws   <- 5000L     # MR multiplier draws         (keep ~2000)

save_rds <- identical(run_mode, "batch") && !is.null(rds_path)  # write only when running a batch
# Refuse to overwrite a git-tracked bundle (committed bundles are read-only;
# guard from the cell-7 campaign-tag incident,
# REPORT_complement_refinements_gate2_2026-09-06.md).  git ls-files
# --error-unmatch exits 1 for an untracked path and non-zero outside a
# repository; both fall through to "not tracked", so an untracked batch
# behaves exactly as before.
.refuse_if_tracked <- function(path) {
  tracked <- tryCatch(
    system2("git", c("ls-files", "--error-unmatch", shQuote(path)),
            stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE) == 0L,
    error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (isTRUE(tracked))
    stop("refusing to overwrite the git-tracked bundle '", path,
         "': committed bundles are read-only -- use a new campaign_tag.",
         call. = FALSE)
  invisible(path)
}

# FB is the wall-clock bottleneck.  forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() itself
# requires nb_boots >= 1 (it errors otherwise), so a skip is enforced HERE -- the
# bootstrap is simply never called -- rather than by passing 0L/NULL into it.
# nb_boots = 0L (or NULL) => run_fb = FALSE => MR-only run.
run_fb <- is.numeric(nb_boots) && length(nb_boots) == 1L && nb_boots >= 1L
run_smoke    <- TRUE      # master flag; FALSE short-circuits the run loop


# ── DGM: León M1 cell (GBSG AFT super-population, alt hypothesis) ───────────
# dgm_model is read from FS_S7_DGM above (it tags the stem, so it has to be);
# unset it resolves to "alt", the former literal.
analysis_time   <- 84     # administrative censoring (months)
cens_adjust     <- log(1.5)
n_super         <- 100000L  # fixed super-population = the eligible-patient universe; trials AND beta(Hhat) draw from this one pool

# ── Subgroup-identification method ─────────────────────────────────────────
# The FB bootstrap (H2, León Eq.7) re-runs whichever engine fs.est used,
# regenerating the candidate family on each resample, so the FB-vs-MR
# comparison is produced for every engine.  Interpretation differs by engine:
# for "consistency" the family is fixed, so FB and MR target the same
# estimand and should agree (the dfbeta-linearisation check); for "dina"/"grf"
# the family regenerates per resample, so FB is the *unconditional*
# comparator against MR's *conditional-on-family* estimate, and a
# FB<->MR gap is the family-regeneration signal, not an error.

grf_selection   <- "frontier"      # only if subgroup_method == "grf": "tree" | "frontier"
grf_select_statistic <- "effect"   # only if grf frontier: "dr" | "effect" (no-op for tree)
grf_depth       <- 2L              # GRF policy-tree depth / max frontier conjunctions
dmin.grf        <- 0.0             # GRF DR-score screening floor
dina_args       <- list()          # extra args forwarded to the DINA selector (dina_args =)
dina_select_statistic <- "effect"  # only if subgroup_method == "dina": "dina" | "effect"

# ── Search configuration (León tuning; resample identification) ────────────
# sg_focus and subgroup_method are set earlier, with the output stem they feed.
consistency_method <- "resample"   # decided: resample identification (the new default)
# MR's de-biasing rule is no longer set explicitly: forestsearch() derives it from
# sg_focus ("maxcons" for the consistency engine), reproducing the legacy
# value while staying faithful per engine.  Override via `reselection =` in
# mr_inference_args (advanced use only).
selection_rule     <- "neighborhood"  # effMaxSG/effMinSG band rule.  INERT under
                                      # sg_focus = "maxcons", whose key is
                                      # consistency-primary with no band term.
                                      # Retained unchanged so the effMaxSG/effMinSG
                                      # arms can use it.
# Part B (1b): what the package already requires (.validate_selection_rule(),
# R/subgroup_consistency_helpers.R:743), checked here so it fails before any
# replicate runs rather than inside every one.
if (!identical(selection_rule, "neighborhood") && !sg_focus %in% .band_foci)
  stop(sprintf("selection_rule = '%s' is accepted only for %s; sg_focus = '%s'.",
               selection_rule, paste(.band_foci, collapse = " / "), sg_focus),
       call. = FALSE)
stop_threshold     <- NULL            # early stopping.  NULL is what this config
                                      # already resolves to: forestsearch() resets
                                      # it for the canonical "hr" family, which
                                      # "maxcons" normalizes to, and does so WITHOUT
                                      # warning unless supplied explicitly.  Named
                                      # here so the setting is inspectable.
# effect_neighborhood: read above (FS_S7_NBHD, default 0.10 = the package
# default) next to the stem it tags; band half-width for effMaxSG/effMinSG,
# inert under sg_focus = "maxcons"/"maxeffCons".
hr_threshold       <- thr_c1        # FS_S7_C1, default 0.90 (read with the stem it tags)
hr_consistency     <- thr_c2        # FS_S7_C2, default 0.80
pconsistency       <- 0.90
fs_splits          <- 400L         # moot under "resample" (closed-form, not literal split)
maxk               <- 2L
n_min              <- NULL
d0_min             <- 10L
d1_min             <- 10L
# RESTORED (were commented out): the consistency `method_args` block below
# references all three UNCONDITIONALLY, and it is built OUTSIDE the tryCatch
# around forestsearch(), so a missing symbol here escaped as an error from
# record_replicate() itself.  Every replicate was then dropped
# (.errorhandling = "remove" in "sims" mode, the outer tryCatch in "boots"),
# leaving results = NULL -- a configuration failure reading as a scientific
# null, and surfacing ~400 lines later as "incorrect number of dimensions".
# Values are the package defaults and match the committed MD harness.
use_lasso          <- FALSE
use_dina           <- FALSE
use_grf            <- FALSE         # FALSE = LASSO-only (fast, "FSl"); set TRUE for "FSlg"
use_twostage       <- TRUE

fs_conf_force      <- c("meno == 0", "er <= 0", "pgr <= 0")   # premenopausal (raw analog of z3 == 1)
fs_conf.cont_jcuts <- list(er = er_jcuts)   # J-quantile grid on raw ER (analog of z1; now meaningful, ER is continuous); J from FS_S7_ER_JCUTS (default 10)

# ── MR inference controls (mr_inference_args) ───────────────────────────────
# Exposed as explicit knobs rather than an inline list, so the harm-confirmation
# rule is visible and changeable.  See @sec-definitions for what these do.
#
#   mr_t_confirm    Harm-confirmation threshold on the EFFECT scale (not the
#                   working log scale).  NULL uses the package's near-null
#                   default: 1 for ratio measures (HR/OR/RR/IRR), 0 for
#                   differences (MD/RD).  Set it NEAR THE NULL rather than at
#                   the screening threshold -- fs_mr_inference()'s own
#                   documentation warns that the de-biasing correction
#                   over-shrinks true effects, so a screening-level threshold
#                   would reject genuine subgroups.
#   mr_confirm_rule "point" tests the de-biased point estimate against
#                   t_confirm; "ci" tests the one-sided 95% selection-adjusted
#                   LOWER bound and is therefore strictly more conservative.
# THE task's knob delta: ci_method = "field".  fs_mr_inference() computes
# everything the "ij" path computes -- the debiased element keeps the IJ
# interval, so the mr_* (IJ) recorder columns are IDENTICAL to an "ij" run --
# and additionally returns the field-calibrated block (fit$mr_inference$field),
# recorded below as the fld_H_* columns.  The field's Monte Carlo sizes
# field_R_out/field_R_in are NOT forwarded by forestsearch() (Stage 0 report,
# finding under 0a), so the package defaults 1000/500 apply; decision F4 of the
# task pins those defaults for this study.
mr_ci_method    <- "field"    # "ij" | "wald" | "field"
mr_t_confirm    <- NULL       # NULL -> near-null default for this measure
mr_confirm_rule <- "point"    # "point" | "ci"
# Uniform (kappa) calibration knob (TASK_mr_field_uniform_2026-09-05): when
# TRUE the gate additionally runs the kappa(Sigma-hat) sweep and the recorder
# captures the fld_H_kappa/... columns below.  FALSE leaves every output
# byte-identical to a pre-uniform render (add-only, default off).
mr_field_uniform <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_UNIFORM", "FALSE"), "TRUE")
# Complement field knob (TASK_mr_field_complement_2026-09-06): when TRUE the
# gate additionally evaluates the field block for the complement Hhat^c --
# same outer/inner draws and winners as the harm field, the complement's own
# influence -- with the one-sided UPPER bound as the primary product (the
# benefit-claim orientation), and the recorder captures the fld_Hc_* columns
# below.  FALSE leaves every output byte-identical to a pre-complement render.
# DEFAULT ON from TASK_cert20_2026-09-08 Part D: the complement bound is one
# of the recommended constructions, so unset = recommended; set
# FS_S7_FIELD_COMPLEMENT=FALSE for the prior behaviour.
mr_field_complement <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_FIELD_COMPLEMENT", "TRUE"), "TRUE")
# IJ residual knob (TASK_complement_refinements_2026-09-06): which residual
# populates the REPORTED mr_*_se_ij / mr_*_lo / mr_*_hi.  "two_term" (default)
# keeps those columns byte-identical; the winner-only and winner-floor SEs
# are recorded alongside (mr_*_se_w / _se_wf and their bounds) whatever the
# knob, so one run evaluates all three.  The joint (H lower, Hc upper) pair
# (fld_joint_*) needs the complement field on.
mr_ij_residual <- .env_chr("FS_S7_IJ_RESIDUAL", "two_term")
stopifnot(mr_ij_residual %in% c("two_term", "winner", "winner_floor"))
# Complement-field scale decomposition knob (TASK_field_studentize_stage1_e0_
# 2026-09-08, Stage 1): when TRUE the gate attaches the add-only
# field$complement$decomp_fields scalars (selected complement's influence-norm
# scale, the outer winners' mean scale and CV, their ratio rho^c) and the
# recorder captures the fld_Hc_scale_* columns below.  FALSE (default) leaves
# every pre-existing column byte-identical; TRUE leaves every pre-existing
# column identical too (the block reads existing objects only).
mr_field_decompose <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_FIELD_DECOMP", "FALSE"), "TRUE")
# Studentized complement field knob (TASK_field_studentize_e1_2026-09-08):
# "none" (default) or "selected" -> fs_mr_inference(field_scale_complement).
# Under "selected" the gate attaches the field-s companions (est2_s,
# upper_1s_s, ... , se_field_s; joint_s) beside the unscaled complement field
# and the recorder captures the fld_Hc_*_s / fld_joint_s_* columns below.
# Add-beside: every pre-existing column is identical under either value.
# DEFAULT "selected" from TASK_cert20_2026-09-08 Part D: field-s is the
# recommended complement construction, so unset = recommended; set
# FS_S7_FIELD_SCALEC=none for the prior behaviour.
mr_field_scalec <- .env_chr("FS_S7_FIELD_SCALEC", "selected")
stopifnot(mr_field_scalec %in% c("none", "selected"))
# Field re-selection recovery knob (TASK_field_recovery_2026-09-09): when TRUE
# the gate attaches the add-only field$recovery list -- membership agreement of
# each outer draw's re-selection against the OBSERVED subgroup, in the CV
# cross-tab vocabulary (sens_H / ppv_H / sens_Hc / npv_Hc) plus the containment
# quantiles -- and the recorder captures the fld_recov_* columns below.  These
# are descriptive: computed from draws already made, no new fits, no new
# randomness, and no construction reads them, so every pre-existing column is
# identical under either value.  FALSE (default) leaves the columns all NA.
mr_field_recovery <- identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_FIELD_RECOV", "FALSE"), "TRUE")

# t_confirm is omitted from the list when NULL so the package resolves its own
# measure-aware default rather than receiving an explicit NULL.
# return_reselection = TRUE (TASK_p30sg_nb20_2026-09-07): the gate's return
# gains its per-draw re-selection frequencies p-hat over the kept family
# (fs_mr_inference.R, `reselection` element); nothing in the arithmetic
# depends on the switch, so every computed value is unchanged.  Recorded
# below as the p_hat_* columns.  As of TASK_cert20_2026-09-08 Part D this is
# also the package default, so the setting below restates the recommendation
# rather than overriding it; it is kept explicit so a render is pinned
# whatever the installed package's default happens to be.  FS_S7_RETURN_RESEL
# exists so the pre-flip behaviour stays reachable from the committed template
# by env alone (Gate D(iii) of TASK_cert20_2026-09-08); unset = recommended.
mr_return_reselection <- !identical(.env_chr("FS_S7_RETURN_RESEL", "TRUE"), "FALSE")
mr_inference_args <- c(
  list(ci_method = mr_ci_method, draws = mr_draws, include_complement = TRUE,
       confirm_rule = mr_confirm_rule, field_uniform = mr_field_uniform,
       field_complement = mr_field_complement, ij_residual = mr_ij_residual,
       field_decompose = mr_field_decompose,
       field_scale_complement = mr_field_scalec,
```
